correctness.rationale: An independent unit-rate lattice walk has H_n/n² ⇒ H with H=Z^-2. The integrated iid-refresh rate clock satisfies Λ_(n^(2α)t)/n² ⇒ (ct)^(1/α)U_α by its exact Laplace-product formula. Independence and the continuous comparison probability imply the full hitting-time weak law. Reflection gives the sine-transform survival curve; Gaussian and stable negative moments give the explicit Mellin formula. A uniform random-walk heat-kernel hitting bound combined with the gamma integral gives survival ≤constant v^(-1/(2α)) uniformly in n, which proves convergence of every subcritical positive moment. Dominated convergence gives the limiting tail coefficient and gamma divergence gives the sharp moment boundary. A standalone numerical checker compared exact finite-n spectral integrals to limits for distinct indices and verified the known q=1 constant; these finite computations are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with the same-model Levit--Reuveni 2026 manuscript identifies established finite-distance spectral survival, heavy-tail exponent and a single large-distance mean, but no complete large-distance law and general fractional-moment convergence. The general classic subordination framework and earlier random-diffusivity analyses were credited; searches for equivalent, broader and dominating claims did not return a matching precise theorem. The originality conclusion is qualified by the possibility of a general unindexed stable-clock theorem.
residual_risks: General stable subordination and random time-change invariance principles are classical and could encompass the weak-limit result as a corollary.
The source exact spectral formula already contains the finite-distance transform; mathematical novelty lies in scaling limit, moment convergence, and explicit full limiting spectrum.
A broader unindexed theorem proving uniform fractional-moment convergence or the same specialization remains a publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 source identifies a phase transition to finite mean and presents a first-moment distance asymptotic but leaves the entire law of large-distance search times unspecified. The proposed theorem gives a universal nondegenerate scaling law, a computable survival curve and a sharp continuum of fractional-moment boundaries even in the infinite-mean regime, directly clarifying what typical and rare search times mean beyond the single mean. This is a motivated structural stochastic-dynamics extension, not an arbitrary parameter substitution.
